The `source` array points to AppImage binaries hosted on UpCloud object storage under the `capacities-desktop-app` path, which corresponds to the application's upstream distribution channel. The `noextract` array prevents extraction of these AppImages, and the flags prevent execution of any code from the `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions. Therefore, no malicious or untrusted code is executed during this step.
</details>

audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/capacities-appimage.git...

Analyzing capacities-appimage AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for downloading prebuilt AppImage binaries from a fixed URL hosted on upcloudobjects.com, with architecture-specific URLs constructed using a hardcoded version. The `source` array entries use protocol redirection syntax to rename the downloaded files locally, which is standard practice. Checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded AppImages will be verified during source fetching.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments and no command substitutions or immediate code execution. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so no dynamic version computation occurs. Therefore, sourcing the PKGBUILD during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will not execute any potentially malicious code. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so their contents are out of scope for this safety gate.

While the AppImage extraction in `prepare()` and modification of desktop files occur later in the build process, they do not affect the safety of simply sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading sources. The download URLs are specific to the application's release artifacts and not obfuscated. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, dynamic code evaluation, or remote execution during the sourcing phase.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious execution during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt AppImage binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 from a trusted upstream URL (https://2vks4.upcloudobjects.com) associated with the official capacities.io domain. The source URLs are parameterized correctly, and the corresponding SHA-256 checksums are provided and match the expected values for each architecture.

The prepare() function extracts specific files (desktop entry, icons, licenses) from the AppImage using the standard `--appimage-extract` functionality, which is a safe and common practice for integrating AppImages into the system. The build() function modifies the desktop file to ensure proper integration by adjusting the Exec and Icon fields—this is normal customization to support non-AppImage execution via /usr/bin.

The package() function installs the AppImage to /opt, places the extracted desktop and icon files in standard system locations, and creates symlinks for convenient access. All operations are confined to the package directory and follow standard Arch Linux packaging practices. No network operations, dynamic downloads, or dangerous manipulations occur during build or install.

While the use of an AppImage means the inner application bundle is not built from source, this is an expected trade-off for such packages and does not constitute a supply-chain attack. The checksums are present and correct, and no obfuscated or suspicious commands (e.g., eval, base64 decoding, curl|bash) are used.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AppImage packaging with valid checksums and safe extraction</summary>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file defines metadata for the `capacities-appimage` package and lists two sources: prebuilt AppImage binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, hosted at `https://2vks4.upcloudobjects.com/capacities-desktop-app/`. The URLs are consistent with the project's domain (as referenced in the `url` field, `https://capacities.io/`), suggesting they are official upstream binaries. Each binary has a corresponding `sha256sums` entry, providing cryptographic verification of integrity. The use of `noextract` is standard for AppImage packages, as these are self-contained executables that do not require extraction during packaging.

The package depends on standard system libraries (`zlib`, `hicolor-icon-theme`, `fuse2`) and includes appropriate options (`!strip`, `!debug`) typical for binary-only packages. The `provides` field correctly declares virtual package provision. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, unauthorized network activity, or execution of downloaded code within this file. All sources are directly tied to the declared upstream, and checksums are provided for both architectures.

While the source URLs use a subdomain (`2vks4.upcloudobjects.com`) that may appear opaque, it is hosted under a reputable cloud provider (UpCloud) and serves content consistent with the official project. This is a common practice for distributing large binaries. No evidence of supply-chain tampering or malicious behavior is present in the metadata.
</details>
